# Martialis

> Martialis is a sourced reference database of martial arts lineages: who
> learned what from whom, which styles relate to which, under what
> organizations, at what places.

## Scope

Martialis covers seven entity types: Person, Style, Organization, Place
(training venues), Source (bibliographic records), Event, and Ranking
system. Persons are the core lineage graph; everything else gives their
relationships context and evidence. Martialis records lineage and
provenance: it does not model pedagogy, curricula, technique taxonomies,
or developmental claims about training.

## Machine-Readable Data

The record format is defined once in `model/martialis.yaml` (LinkML), from which
the JSON-LD context, the OWL ontology, the structural SHACL shapes and the seven
per-type JSON Schemas are generated. The vocabulary namespace is
`https://w3id.org/martialis/ontology#`; the SKOS controlled-vocabulary namespace
is `https://w3id.org/martialis/vocab/<scheme-slug>`, with every scheme in the
single file `ontology/vocabularies.ttl`. Concept-valued fields are authored as
scheme-prefixed CURIEs (`placeclass:dojo`, `conflevel:probable`), which the
context expands to the concept IRI.

Canonical artifacts:

- Ontology (OWL, Turtle): [https://w3id.org/martialis/ontology](https://w3id.org/martialis/ontology) (content-negotiated; ask for text/turtle), [https://martial.is/ontology.ttl](https://martial.is/ontology.ttl), or [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Martial-IS/martialis-db/main/ontology/martialis.ttl](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Martial-IS/martialis-db/main/ontology/martialis.ttl)
- SHACL shapes (structural, blocking): [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Martial-IS/martialis-db/main/ontology/martialis.shacl.ttl](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Martial-IS/martialis-db/main/ontology/martialis.shacl.ttl)
- SHACL shapes (quality, informational): [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Martial-IS/martialis-db/main/ontology/martialis-quality.shacl.ttl](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Martial-IS/martialis-db/main/ontology/martialis-quality.shacl.ttl)
- SKOS controlled vocabularies: [https://w3id.org/martialis/vocab](https://w3id.org/martialis/vocab) or `ontology/vocabularies.ttl` in this repository
- JSON-LD context: [https://martial.is/context.jsonld](https://martial.is/context.jsonld) or [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Martial-IS/martialis-db/main/schemas/context.jsonld](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Martial-IS/martialis-db/main/schemas/context.jsonld)
- Full RDF export (Turtle): [https://martial.is/data.ttl](https://martial.is/data.ttl) or [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Martial-IS/martialis-db/main/export/data.ttl](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Martial-IS/martialis-db/main/export/data.ttl)
- Bibliography (CSL-JSON, one record per Source): [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Martial-IS/martialis-db/main/export/sources.csl.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Martial-IS/martialis-db/main/export/sources.csl.json)
- Ontology and SHACL documentation: [https://w3id.org/martialis/ontology](https://w3id.org/martialis/ontology), [https://w3id.org/martialis/ontology/validation](https://w3id.org/martialis/ontology/validation), [https://w3id.org/martialis/ontology/quality](https://w3id.org/martialis/ontology/quality)
- Landing page linking to all of the above: [https://martial.is/model](https://martial.is/model)

## Interpretation Rules

- Confidence level and the evidence analysis (Mills: source classification,
  information type, evidence type) are curator judgments about how well a
  claim is sourced, not about a person's skill, legitimacy, or standing. A
  refuted, doubtful or contested lineage claim is presented and marked, not
  removed.
- `martialis:possiblySameAs` links candidate identities without asserting
  they are the same person; it is weaker than `owl:sameAs`, not identity.
- `martialis:variantOf` (a named variant within one art) is distinct from
  `stylerel:derived_from` (crosses into a different art). Only
  `variant_of` is materialized as a direct edge; read the other four
  style-relation types from the `StyleRelationAssertion` itself.
- Every claim is a first-class `martialis:Assertion` node carrying
  `martialis:hasConfidence` (an ordered level, assessing agent, rationale) and
  `martialis:hasEvidence` (one or more `martialis:SourceAssertionRelation`
  nodes with source, `supports`, locator, quotation). A contested
  claim carries a `supports: false` source; a refuted one is assessed
  `conflevel:refuted`.
- Convenience edges (`wasTaughtBy`/`teaches`, `taughtAt`, `trainedAt`,
  `variantOf`/`hasVariant`, `parentOrg`, `possiblySameAs`,
  `org:ChangeEvent`, `prov:wasDerivedFrom`/`prov:wasAttributedTo`) are
  materialized at export time from the underlying assertions; a doubtful or
  refuted assertion gives none of them except the PROV-O ones. A possible,
  probable or confirmed one gives the same edge, so follow an edge back to
  its assertion for the sourcing and the confidence.
- A `martialis:TeacherAssertion` with no `martialis:teacher` records training
  under an unidentified teacher: a teacher existed, but no source names them.
  It materializes `trainedAt`, never `wasTaughtBy`/`teaches`.
- A claim sourced only from a single encyclopedia-style tertiary source is
  surfaced in the quality tier and is not disqualifying.
- Do not infer a person's skill, rank equivalence across styles, or the
  legitimacy of one lineage over another. Martialis records claims and their
  evidence; it does not adjudicate martial arts authority.

CC-BY-SA-4.0, CC0-1.0 respectively), and the maker asserts the EU sui generis
database right over the data and licenses it under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Full text:
[https://github.com/Martial-IS/martialis-db/blob/main/LICENSING.md](https://github.com/Martial-IS/martialis-db/blob/main/LICENSING.md)

Attribution is a condition of CC-BY-SA-4.0; LICENSING.md says when it applies.
When you share or present database content, credit Martialis and link to the URI
of each record you use, in this form:
`<record name>, Martialis (https://martial.is/entity/<ULID>), CC BY-SA 4.0`.
Quotations and linked media stay with their rightsholders, and some description
text comes from Wikipedia under CC BY-SA. The maker reserves its own text and data
mining right under Art. 4 of Directive (EU) 2019/790 over the data, in every copy.
Art. 3 research use is unaffected.
